spec.full_target: Let n,m be positive integers; u:R^n×(0,∞)→R^m jointly smooth, q unit. Assume |u|=1, u_tt−Δ_xu=a u pointwise, and u=q outside a compact set uniformly on every compact time interval. Define e=|u_t|²+Σ|∂_xj u|² and E=∫R^n e dx. Prove integrability of e, differentiability of E, and E'=0 at every r>0.
spec.conclusion: For every r>0, e(·,r) is Lebesgue integrable, E is differentiable at r, and E'(r)=0.

propositions.statement: For every r>0, e(·,r) is Lebesgue integrable, E is differentiable at r, and E'(r)=0.

argument.text: Fix r>0; choose J and C_J using H003. Derivatives vanish off the common support and by continuity on the boundary. Thus e is continuous compactly supported; M001 proves integrability. Choose box B containing C_J. M004 gives uniform continuity of e_t on B×J. M002 gives the difference quotient of e as an average of e_t; uniform convergence and finite measure prove E'(r)=∫_B e_t.

Differentiate e. For g_j=u_t·u_j, ∂_j g_j=(∂_j u_t)·u_j+u_t·u_jj; it is continuous compactly supported and integrable by M001. M003 gives Fubini after coordinate permutation; M002 gives zero integral of ∂_j g_j by endpoint values on a large interval. Hence E'=2∫u_t·(u_tt−Δu). Differentiating H001 gives u·u_t=0, and H002 says acceleration is a multiple of u, so integrand zero. Thus E'=0. Since r arbitrary, conclusion follows.
